Methodology & definitions

SERIES NOTES

How vendor totals are grouped

Figures on this page come from the New York City Record Recent Contract Awards dataset (NYC Open Data qyyg-4tf5), limited to awards in Construction categories. Many firms appear under several spellings of their name, and a single firm group can file under more than one legal entity. Where we can confirm by hand that several names belong to the same firm, we group them under one parent total and list every underlying name and its amount, so nothing is hidden. Grouping is a fixed, verified list of name variants, not automated name-matching or any statistical guess. We group only on a distinctive shared identifier or an unmistakable spelling variation of the same company; when a connection is uncertain, we leave the names separate. Each amount is the value stated in the award notice, which is a floor rather than a running total of work performed or paid, so a group's total is a lower bound. This dataset covers City-agency awards only. Work let by the MTA, the School Construction Authority, the Port Authority, and New York State agencies is out of scope here because those datasets do not name the awarded contractor.

A note for credit work

This is the public demand-side view of a contractor: what the City has hired it to do. It says nothing about costs, margins, bonding capacity, or performance. Treat it as one input alongside financials, not a substitute for them.
